label: Twofold cost of sex
statement_en: An asexual mutant female in a sexual population with equal sex ratio produces twice as many grandchildren as a sexual female, so sex needs a compensating advantage of up to twofold to persist.

hypotheses.name: maynardsmith-twofold-cost#assumed-1
hypotheses.statement: Anisogamy: males contribute nothing to offspring number or survival.

hypotheses.name: maynardsmith-twofold-cost#assumed-2
hypotheses.statement: Equal fecundity and viability of sexual and asexual females and of their daughters.

hypotheses.name: maynardsmith-twofold-cost#assumed-3
hypotheses.statement: Primary sex ratio exactly 1:1 in sexual broods; discrete non-overlapping generations; infinite population (deterministic fractions).

scope.basis: a theorem about a model: it applies wherever the design supplies the quantities it uses and accepts the hypotheses in scope.assumed
kernelChecked: For 0 < q < 1 and fecundity f > 0 the odds of asexual to sexual females satisfy odds(q_next) = 2 odds(q), and f cancels.
Iterated n generations the odds are 2^n times the initial odds.
